Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test is for the method setModifyJavaTime(Date) in the class X5455_ExtendedTimestamp. The test attempts to set a modification time using a Java Date object that represents a value too large to fit in the allowed 32-bit timestamp range. The test expects an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown, which should be triggered if the timestamp value can't fit in 32 bits.

Looking at the code, setModifyJavaTime(Date d) calls dateToZipLong(Date d), which converts the Date into a ZipLong representation by dividing the Java time in milliseconds by 1000 to get seconds, then calling unixTimeToZipLong(long l). The unixTimeToZipLong method verifies that the long value fits in 32 bits (allows values less than 2^32) and throws IllegalArgumentException if it doesn't.

The bug report mentions the failure under JDK 9 due to a "bogus value from getTime()." The root cause is likely a change in how Date.getTime() behaves or is interpreted under JDK 9, possibly related to time zone, precision, or overflow issues. Because the test expects an exception when the time is too large, but the failure occurs, it suggests the check might be bypassing or improperly validating, potentially because the division or value isn't what is expected under the new JDK.

The underlying issue is that the test relies on exact behavior of Date.getTime() and Unix time conversion, but JDK 9 changes have caused it to break, leading to the test failure. This matches the report's note about JDK-8073497 affecting this behavior.

Recent bug reports retrieved do not seem directly related, as they address other parts of the codebase or earlier JDK compatibility issues.

To fix the problem, the code handling Date to Unix time conversion (dateToZipLong and unixTimeToZipLong) and the validation that throws the exception need to be scrutinized and adapted to the new JDK behavior, possibly with extra checks or fixes in time handling or the test expectations.

Next, suggest which methods to fix.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.setModifyJavaTime(java.util.Date)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.dateToZipLong(java.util.Date)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.X5455_ExtendedTimestamp.unixTimeToZipLong(long)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
